Edward Park gets straight to it. // Edward Park: We're putting together our coverage of the selectboard member race. Can I get you on the record? [Replies: Who else are you talking to? | Sure. Set it up. | I'll pass on this one. | Let me look at my week and call you back.] // Edward Park: FIONA CABRERA
Who else are you talking to?
Where you stand on the questions people in South Barre care about, and why you're running. [Replies: I'll do it. Tell me when. | I'd rather let the campaign speak for itself. | I have to go. Call me later.] // Edward Park: FIONA CABRERA

Good. I'll send the questions over.

01.words: Folks, thank you very much. I'm hopeful today, and I think you've got reason to be too. Everybody who's had this job walked into problems they didn't make. The job is fixing them anyway. // It's a new day, and I think we could all use a little more hope than we've had lately. I took that oath feeling good about it, because I think this country can do a lot more than we've been asking of it.

07.words:
First thing on January 23rd, Kevin Farmer is waiting for you downtown.
Kevin Farmer spoke against the governor's asks in front of everyone. In the hallway they are quieter, and watching your face. // Kevin Farmer: Fiona, a word. I answered the governor today, and I wanted you to hear why from me.
The governor asked for a lot today. Are you with the governor, or with us? [Replies: Some of it I liked and some of it I didn't. I'm not going to pretend it was all one thing. | How much of that was for the cameras? | If your side brings me something real, I'll read it with an open mind. | No. Not on the day of the speech.] // Kevin Farmer: FIONA CABRERA
Some of it I liked and some of it I didn't. I'm not going to pretend it was all one thing.
I'll keep making the case, with you or without you. [Replies: The governor has a point on a few things. I'm not ready to say which. | I'm not picking a side in a hallway. | Let's pick this up another time, when it's quieter.] // Kevin Farmer: FIONA CABRERA
The governor has a point on a few things. I'm not ready to say which.
The governor's asks will come back to us as bills, and we'll have to vote on every one. [Replies: I heard the same speech you did. I'll judge each ask when it comes up as a bill. | I'll vote the way my district needs, not the way either of you asks. | I have to get to my next meeting.] // Kevin Farmer: FIONA CABRERA
I heard the same speech you did. I'll judge each ask when it comes up as a bill.
Think about who sent you here. They heard that speech too.
Thank you for the minute. I know the day was long.

Ivan Maldonado: First thing on November 27th, you head to the City Clerk's office to pick up the papers for Selectboard member. Ivan Maldonado pulls them from a drawer. // Ivan Maldonado: What can I do for you? [Replies: I want to run for Selectboard member. March 3, 2026 · Held by Tammy Wooten] // Ivan Maldonado: FIONA CABRERA
I want to run for Selectboard member.
Running for Selectboard member? Good. Let me pull the papers. There's no primary for this one, so you'd go straight onto the ballot March 3, 2026. You'd have a seat on the Barre Town Selectboard, voting on the budget and every ordinance that comes before it. It all has to be back to me by January 26, 2026. [Replies: I'm in. Give me the papers.] // FIONA CABRERA
I'm in. Give me the papers.

09.words:
First thing on November 28th, you sit down at home with Amy Cabrera.
Amy Cabrera sits down across from you. // Amy Cabrera: Fiona, sit down a second.
Tammy Wooten is running for selectboard member too. I wanted you to hear it from me. [Replies: Do you know much about Tammy Wooten? | Then I'd better get to work. | Let them run. | Thanks for telling me.] // Amy Cabrera: FIONA CABRERA
Do you know much about Tammy Wooten?
Not much. Only what was filed. [Replies: Good. Now it's a real race. | Doesn't change anything for me. | I need a minute.] // Amy Cabrera: FIONA CABRERA
Good. Now it's a real race.
Good. We're behind you.
